title_en: Luo Lunfu v. Determination of Liability for Road Traffic Accident
keywords_en: Administrative; Determination of liability for road traffic accidents; Second instance (appeal); Intermediate People's Court; Sichuan Province; Natural person; State organ; Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; Regulations on Road Traffic Management of the People's Republic of China; Measures for Handling Road Traffic Accidents; Whether determination of liability for road traffic accidents falls within the scope of administrative litigation; Whether the facts of liability determination are clear and the evidence is sufficient; Reversal of judgment; Traffic accident; Road construction; Liability determination; Administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Luo Lunfu v. Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident

Plaintiff: Luo Lunfu, female, born on May 22, 1955, a native of Lu County, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Third Brigade of the Traffic Police Detachment of the Luzhou Public Security Bureau, Sichuan Province.

The plaintiff, Luo Lunfu, brought an administrative lawsuit before the Longmatan District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province, against the determination of liability for a road traffic accident made by the defendant, the Third Brigade of the Traffic Police Detachment of the Luzhou Public Security Bureau, Sichuan Province (hereinafter referred to as the Traffic Police Brigade), concerning her son Kang Zhonghua (deceased).

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant Traffic Police Brigade failed to add the road construction unit that was working on the accident site as a party liable for the traffic accident, and instead, by Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident, determined that the driver Kang Zhonghua bore full responsibility for the traffic accident. This determination of liability contradicts the facts recorded in the defendant's on-site inspection record and interrogation records, which indicate that at the construction site on the road where the accident occurred, there were no warning signs, protective barriers, and the personnel on duty had left work early. The decision is unclear in facts and insufficient in evidence, constituting an illegal specific administrative act. The plaintiff requests that the defendant's determination of liability for the traffic accident be revoked, and that the defendant be ordered to make a new determination of liability for this road traffic accident.

Evidence submitted by the plaintiff to the court: 1. Testimony records of witnesses Xiao Anliang, Liang Kaiji, and Chen Yanxi, proving that during construction, the construction section allowed only one-way traffic, and measures taken included designated personnel at designated posts on duty from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., but at the time of the accident no one was on duty. 2. On-site inspection record of the traffic accident, proving that a large amount of carbon slag was piled on the road surface of the construction section at the accident site.

Defendant's Defense: If the plaintiff disagrees with the determination of liability for the road traffic accident, she may only apply for a re-determination to the traffic police department at the next higher level within the statutory 15-day period. The plaintiff did not apply for re-determination, and moreover, she agreed to mediation by the defendant regarding damages for the accident and reached a mediation agreement. If the plaintiff now files an administrative lawsuit with the court, the disagreement can only be with the "mediation agreement." According to Article 1, Paragraph 2, Item (3) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law Interpretation) (Fa Shi [2000] No. 8), effective from March 10, 2000, mediation acts do not fall within the scope of administrative litigation. Therefore, the plaintiff's lawsuit should be dismissed.

Evidence submitted by the defendant to the court: 1. Written mediation agreement on damages for road traffic accident, mediation record for road traffic accident, and service certificate of the Third Brigade of the Luzhou Traffic Police, proving that the plaintiff had accepted the determination of liability for the road traffic accident and had reached a mediation agreement on damages. 2. Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident, sketch map of on-site investigation of the traffic accident, and on-site diagram of the road traffic accident, proving that the road surface at the accident site was 11.90 meters wide, the piled materials occupied approximately 6.45 meters of the road width, leaving 5.45 meters of road width, and vehicles could pass safely. 3. Report of Luzhou Shulu Road Industry Co., Ltd. on the Road Surface Reconstruction from Songtan Bridge to Yangguan Bridge on the Lulong Road, proving that the construction unit's road surface reconstruction was approved by the Traffic Police Detachment of the Luzhou Public Security Bureau, and the procedures were complete and lawful. 4. Six photographs of construction warning signs set up by the construction unit at both ends of the construction section and photos of the accident scene, proving that the construction unit had installed obvious warning signs and safety facilities at the 38 km mark of the Lulong Road (Longchang to Luzhou direction) and at the 41 km+200 m mark (Luzhou to Longchang direction), in accordance with Article 66, Paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Road Traffic Management (hereinafter referred to as the Road Traffic Management Regulations). 5. Interrogation record of duty personnel Liang Kaiji, proving that warning signs and duty posts were set up at the construction site.

The defendant Traffic Police Brigade had no objection to the two pieces of evidence submitted by the plaintiff Luo Lunfu.

Plaintiff Luo Lunfu had no objection to the defendant Traffic Police Brigade's evidence 1, 2, 3, and 5, but rebutted the defendant's evidence 4 with her own evidence 1.

After trial, the Longmatan District People's Court of Luzhou found: After cross-examination, evidence 1 and 2 submitted by plaintiff Luo Lunfu and evidence 1, 2, 3, and 5 of the defendant Traffic Police Brigade were all acknowledged by both parties and should be admitted; evidence 4 submitted by the Traffic Police Brigade, whose content was consistent with the testimony record of Liang Kaiji in evidence 1 submitted by Luo Lunfu, should also be admitted. Luo Lunfu's assertion that no safety signs were present at the accident scene based on her own evidence could not support her claim that no signs were set up on the entire construction section; Luo Lunfu's argument that the duty personnel at the duty post had left work early and the construction unit should bear responsibility lacked legal basis and was not supported. The Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident made by the Traffic Police Brigade had clear facts, sufficient evidence, correct application of law, and lawful procedures, and was a lawful specific administrative act that should be upheld. Accordingly, the Longmatan District People's Court, in accordance with Article 54, Paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law), rendered judgment on January 26, 2001:

The determination of liability for Kang Zhonghua in the Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident made by the Traffic Police Brigade on October 19, 2000, is upheld.

Plaintiff Luo Lunfu, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Luzhou Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province. Main grounds of appeal: 1. The accident section was not within the scope of road repair, and the construction unit's act of piling a large amount of carbon slag on the bridge was illegal. The appellee's Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident did not determine this fact; 2. The carbon slag piled on the bridge surface in front of where Kang Zhonghua was driving occupied more than half of the road width, without any protective barriers or safety signs, and had a direct impact on the occurrence of the accident. Under such circumstances, the appellee's determination that Kang Zhonghua bore full responsibility for the accident was erroneous. As a result, the appellant was required to bear all compensation costs for the accident, which was unjust. The first-instance judgment was unclear in facts and insufficient in evidence. The appellant requests that on appeal, the first-instance judgment be reversed, the appellee's Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident be revoked, and the appellee be ordered to make a new determination of liability for this accident.

The appellee, the Traffic Police Brigade, did not submit a defense.

After trial, the Luzhou Intermediate People's Court found:

The appellee Traffic Police Brigade, in its Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident made on October 19, 2000, determined that at approximately 21:25 on September 5, 2000, Kang Zhonghua, son of the appellant Luo Lunfu, was driving agricultural vehicle with license plate Chuan E06349 from Longchang to Luzhou. When reaching the construction section at 41 km of the Lulong Road, to avoid piled materials (carbon slag) on the road surface, he drove off the Songtan Bridge surface and fell under the bridge, causing the passenger Li Guihua to die at the scene and Kang Zhonghua to die after unsuccessful rescue at hospital. Kang Zhonghua, due to improper measures leading to the overturn, violated Article 7, Paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Management Regulations. In accordance with Article 19 of the Measures for the Handling of Road Traffic Accidents of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Road Traffic Accident Handling Measures), Kang Zhonghua was determined to bear full responsibility for the accident, and Li Guihua bore no responsibility.

To prove that the Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident was based on clear facts and correct application of law, the appellee Traffic Police Brigade, in addition to submitting evidence for the determination to the first-instance court, also submitted the following legal bases: Article 7, Paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Management Regulations issued by the State Council, which reads: "In situations not provided for in these Regulations, vehicles and pedestrians must proceed under the principle of ensuring safety"; Article 19 of the Road Traffic Accident Handling Measures, which reads: "If a traffic accident is caused by the illegal act of one party, that party shall bear full responsibility, and the other parties shall bear no responsibility." "If a traffic accident is caused jointly by the illegal acts of two parties, the party whose illegal act played a greater role in the accident shall bear primary responsibility, and the other party shall bear secondary responsibility; if the illegal acts played substantially equal roles, both parties shall bear equal responsibility." "If a traffic accident is caused jointly by the illegal acts of three or more parties, responsibility shall be allocated according to the role each party's illegal act played in the accident"; and the Procedures for Handling Road Traffic Accidents issued by the Ministry of Public Security.

Regarding the evidence for the determination submitted by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade, the appellant Luo Lunfu argued that the photos were not taken at the time of the accident, and other evidence did not prove that the road section under repair included the Songtan Bridge where the accident occurred; apart from that, she had no other objections. Luo Lunfu stated that the on-site investigation diagram and on-site inspection record had already proved that the Songtan Bridge was 11.90 meters wide, the piled materials occupied 6.45 meters of the road width, and there were no warning signs or protective barriers in front of the direction the accident vehicle was traveling, leaving no time to avoid, causing one side of the wheels to press on the piled materials, resulting in deviation of direction and then driving off the bridge. Therefore, the on-site situation at the accident had a direct cause with the occurrence of the accident.

The appellant Luo Lunfu had no objection to the legal bases submitted by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade. However, she argued that Article 66 of the Road Traffic Management Regulations clearly provides: "No unit or individual may, without approval from the public security organ, occupy roads to set up stalls, park vehicles, pile materials for work, erect sheds, build houses, conduct market trade, or engage in other activities that obstruct traffic." "If municipal or highway administration departments need to occupy or excavate roads for maintenance, except for routine maintenance and road repair operations, they must consult with the public security organ to jointly adopt traffic maintenance measures before construction; if other units need to excavate roads, they must first obtain consent from the municipal or highway administration department, and then complete procedures with the public security organ." "At construction sites where roads are excavated, obvious signs and safety protective facilities must be set up. After completion, the site must be promptly cleaned, and the road surface and road facilities repaired." The Traffic Police Brigade had no evidence to prove that the piled materials on the Songtan Bridge were lawfully placed by the construction unit.

Regarding the Written Mediation Agreement on Damages for Road Traffic Accident submitted by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade, the appellant Luo Lunfu explained: At that time, she was in grief over the death of her relative and believed that the Traffic Police Brigade would resolve the compensation issue fairly and reasonably in accordance with the law, so she signed the mediation agreement without careful consideration. However, she later believed that the Traffic Police Brigade's determination that she should bear costs including the autopsy fee of RMB 1,000, her vehicle repair fee of RMB 12,813, vehicle parking fee of RMB 360, vehicle rescue fee of RMB 2,080, Songtan Bridge railing repair fee of RMB 720, and green crop compensation fee of RMB 850 from the 19 items of damages was unfair and unreasonable.

After trial, the Luzhou Intermediate People's Court found:

The ground for the appellant Luo Lunfu's challenge to the photos of road conditions submitted by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade, that they were not taken at the scene at the time of the accident, was valid. This evidence had no probative force for the facts of the case and was not admitted; other evidence was valid and should be admitted.

The legal bases submitted by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade were all effective and should be applied. The appellant Luo Lunfu's argument, based on Article 66 of the Road Traffic Management Regulations, that the Traffic Police Brigade had not proved that the carbon slag piled on the Songtan Bridge was lawfully placed by the construction unit, was consistent with the facts of the case and should be accepted. In addition, Article 4 of the Procedures for Handling Road Traffic Accidents issued by the Ministry of Public Security provides: "Traffic police must have at least three years of traffic management practice, pass specialized training and examinations, and obtain a certificate issued by the public security management department of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government before they may handle accidents at or above the general accident level." Whether Lü Helong and Zhang Tie, who handled the serious accident involved in this case, possessed such qualifications was not proved by the Traffic Police Brigade with evidence.

The dispute between the appellant Luo Lunfu and the appellee Traffic Police Brigade over the confirmation and assumption of the compensation amount in the Written Mediation Agreement on Damages for Road Traffic Accident is not the subject of this trial and should be resolved in a separate case.

The determination of liability for a road traffic accident is an administrative confirmation act carried out by the public security organ under the authorization of administrative regulations. This act directly relates to whether, after a road traffic accident, a party has committed a crime and should be investigated for criminal liability, whether the act is illegal and should be subject to administrative penalties, whether the party bears civil compensation liability, or whether the party can obtain civil compensation. Therefore, it involves the rights and obligations of the parties. Article 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law provides: "If a citizen, legal person, or other organization considers that a specific administrative act of an administrative organ or its personnel has infringed upon its lawful rights and interests, it has the right to file a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with this Law." The appellant Luo Lunfu, considering that the Traffic Police Brigade's act of determining liability for the traffic accident infringed upon her lawful rights and interests, filed an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court. This is within the scope of administrative litigation of the People's Court according to law. Based on Luo Lunfu's claims, the object of review in this case is the act of determining liability for the road traffic accident made by the Traffic Police Brigade, not the mediation act of the Traffic Police Brigade. The determination of liability for a road traffic accident is neither a mediation act nor an arbitration act provided by law. The Traffic Police Brigade's argument that this case is not an administrative litigation, based on Article 1, Paragraph 2, Item (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law Interpretation, which provides that "mediation acts and arbitration acts provided by law" do not fall within the scope of administrative litigation, is untenable.

Article 22 of the Road Traffic Accident Handling Measures provides: "If a party disagrees with the determination of liability for a traffic accident, it may, within fifteen days of receiving the written determination of liability for the traffic accident, apply to the public security organ at the next higher level for a re-determination." The provision that the party "may" apply to the higher public security organ for re-determination, rather than "shall," means that applying to the higher public security organ for re-determination is not a prerequisite to administrative reconsideration. Moreover, Article 9 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Reconsideration Law) provides: "If a citizen, legal person, or other organization considers that a specific administrative act has infringed upon its lawful rights and interests, it may apply for administrative reconsideration within sixty days from the date it knows or should know of the specific administrative act; however, if the law provides for a longer period, that period shall apply." Article 42 provides: "If the provisions of laws promulgated before the implementation of this Law concerning administrative reconsideration are inconsistent with those of this Law, the provisions of this Law shall prevail." Even if applying to the higher public security organ for re-determination were understood as a prerequisite to administrative reconsideration, the period for a party to apply for administrative reconsideration should be sixty days, not fifteen days. The appellee Traffic Police Brigade's indication in the Decision on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident that the party should apply for administrative reconsideration within fifteen days was erroneous. The Traffic Police Brigade's argument that the appellant Luo Lunfu did not apply for administrative reconsideration within the statutory fifteen-day period, and therefore the determination of liability for the road traffic accident had already taken legal effect, is untenable.

The serious traffic accident involved in this case occurred on the Songtan Bridge. At the time of the accident, carbon slag was piled on the bridge surface. Whether the bridge surface was within the scope of renovation, whether piling carbon slag was permitted, whether piling carbon slag without setting up safety signs and protective barriers was lawful, and whether this act had a direct causal relationship with the occurrence of this serious traffic accident, were neither determined nor excluded by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade. Therefore, the determination of liability for this accident was unclear in facts. The legal basis applied by the Traffic Police Brigade in making this determination of liability for the road traffic accident was Article 19 of the Road Traffic Accident Handling Measures. This article contains three paragraphs, respectively providing for the determination of liability in cases involving one party, two parties, or three or more parties. The Traffic Police Brigade only generally applied Article 19 of the Road Traffic Accident Handling Measures without specifying which paragraph applied, constituting an error in the application of law.

After a road traffic accident occurs, the public security traffic management department should investigate and collect evidence in accordance with legal procedures to ascertain the cause of the accident. Various factors related to the occurrence of the accident should be fully considered and comprehensively analyzed to accurately allocate accident liability. The determination of liability for the serious traffic accident involved in this case made by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade was unclear in facts, insufficient in evidence, and erroneous in the application of law; this administrative act was not lawful.

In the first-instance trial, although the court presided over the parties' presentation of evidence, cross-examination, and authentication, it failed to identify the legal facts that could be confirmed through trial. It then concluded that the Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident made by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade had clear facts, sufficient evidence, legal procedures, and correct application of law, and upheld this unlawful administrative act. This was erroneous and should be corrected. The appeal of Luo Lunfu had merit and should be accepted.

In summary, the Luzhou Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 54, Paragraph (2), Items 1 and 2 and Article 61, Item (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law, rendered judgment on April 24, 2001:

1. The first-instance administrative judgment is reversed;

2. The Decision No. 2000-279 on Determination of Liability for a Road Traffic Accident made by the appellee Traffic Police Brigade on October 19, 2000, is revoked;

3. The appellee Traffic Police Brigade is ordered to make a new determination of liability for the serious traffic accident that occurred on September 5, 2000, at 41 km of the Lulong Road.
